messages.author: 766402329d5d7c58
messages.subject: rapache permission
parts:
Hi,

I would like to develop a web application that would fetch data from some server, do a little statistical processing and output a graph. I am having problem in choosing where to output the graph to. Basically I need to find a directory where R can write to and apache can read from.

So should I change the permission of the webroot so that R can write to it? How should I do it? this architecture is eventually going to be used in a real deployment so I don't want to do chmod 777 or anything that would be not implementable in a real site because of security issues. Alternatively would it be better to output the graph to some other directory where R can read say /tmp and allow apache to access it? (adding www-data to the /tmp's group in Ubuntu/Debian or whatever equivalent in Centos/Fedora)In that case how would I refer to the path (say /tmp/imgage.png) in a brew script?

I have looked at many threads but all solutions stop short of offering a  concrete example and instead say something like "then find a directory and R can write to and apache can access to output to" without being more specific about it.

Thanks.

P.S. I would like to look at the webapps by Jeroen Ooms but not sure where I can get the source codes. A pointer to that would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: b2a4f8328faaf97f
messages.subject: Re: rapache permission
parts:
Hi bernard,
I avoided that problem in the following way: I added the user of the running Ubuntu session to the www-data group, then chowned everything in the server folder to [user]:www-data with rwx enabled for the group members (chmod 770 or similar. note that this might have to differ for some files iirc.). Now the files that R makes by for example the write() function have [user]:www-data rights and can be called by Apache in another instance.
Adding the user to www-data:
sudo adduser [user] www-data
Changing the permissions in the server folder:
sudo chown [user]:www-data

I suggest that the user running the Apache session does not have admin privileges, so he can't call sudo himself. Maybe have those activated during development but disable the privileges for security reasons when your project goes live.

Hope this helps!

Best regards
Z

messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Re: rapache permission
parts:
On Mon, Jan 20, 2014 at 6:06 PM, bernard <bwberna...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi, Jeroen,
>
> I have read some documentations for opencpu, it seems to be very
> interesting. Does it only work with Ubuntu? What if you want to deploy it on
> a LAMP system running say CENTOS? How does rapache fit in?

Yes, OpenCPU currently only runs on debian/ubuntu because it has several dependencies (apparmor, r) which do not ship with rhel/centos. If for whatever reason all you have is a centos machine, I recommend you install KVM and run a virtual ubuntu server inside centos. This is really quite easy to setup.

> I am probably a bit dense, It is still not clear to me how opencpu handles
> the permission problem which I started this thread about. So say a graph is
> output with tempfile(), how does apache access tempdir() since it is outside
> /var/www?
It uses apparmor, which is a mandatory access control module in the linux kernel, available in debian and ubuntu. See the FAQ and several other resources.

> As I am kind of a novice to this may be I should start studying something
> more basic. I am wondering if I can get the source code for your stock plot
> web application as it seems to be the prototype of what I would like to
> figure out at this moment
> http://www.stat.ucla.edu/~jeroen/stockplot.html
I updated all of that code to an opencpu app: https://github.com/opencpu/stocks. Making apps is really not that difficult. Have a look at this jsfiddle as well: http://jsfiddle.net/opencpu/MkAVF/
